summary: The preregistered continuation-management hypothesis fails. After a strong H1 rejection at Daily S1/R1, four-hour incoming-direction continuation remains approximately flat/slightly positive at +0.0050 ATR, 95% pair-year bootstrap CI [-0.0094,+0.0189], rather than negative. Continuation is weaker than at matched outer strong-wick controls by -0.0106 ATR, but that pivot-specific contrast is not robust, CI [-0.0302,+0.0089]. Development and validation remain positive, only 3/10 pairs are negative, cooldown robustness remains positive, and 2026 YTD stays unopened.

primary_findings.metric: S1/R1 matched outer HOLD4 continuation return
core minus outer HOLD4 continuation return

robustness: A deterministic 4H same-pair/same-direction cooldown leaves S1/R1 core HOLD4 positive at +0.0051 ATR.
Core-minus-outer remains negative under cooldown but its 95% interval still reaches slightly above zero.
The frozen 1H, 2H, 4H and 8H core continuation means are all non-negative; core-minus-outer reverses positive by 8H.
S1 and R1 differ descriptively, but named-side selection was prospectively prohibited as a rescue after pooled failure.
limitations: The study evaluates a generic pre-existing incoming-direction position and intentionally does not model its original entry or accumulated P&L.
2015-2025 is related/exposed pivot research data; only the management decision semantics were newly preregistered.
The result rejects a simple universal EXIT_NOW rule; it does not prove that no more complex risk-management policy could ever have value.
2026 YTD remains unopened and supplies no confirmation evidence here.
authorized_next: Treat S1/R1 rejection as structural/context information only; no deterministic exit instruction is supported.
If pivot research continues, choose a genuinely new market question rather than optimizing this failed management rule.
prohibited_next: Do not optimize partial-exit percentages, trailing stops, management horizons, wick thresholds or pivot-zone widths as a rescue.
Do not mine S1-only, R1-only, session or weekday subsets to reverse the pooled decision.
Do not open 2026 YTD for this failed internal management hypothesis.
Do not create Pine alerts, sizing or live-management rules from this study.
